summary: This is a clipped Hong Kong Observatory page for its 9-day weather forecast, mostly navigation and template placeholders with few concrete values. The substantive content is an explanation of how to read the forecast: temperature and humidity ranges based on 1991-2020 climate data, and the Probability of Significant Rain (PSR) categories. It also states how forecast accuracy declines with lead time and varies by season and weather system.
one_line: Hong Kong Observatory page explaining its 9-day forecast, the Probability of Significant Rain categories, and forecast accuracy by lead time.
key_facts: The 9-day Weather Forecast provides general indications of the trends in weather for the coming 9 days.
For detailed description of today's weather forecast, users should refer to the Local Weather Forecast.

The middle 50% range (between 25th and 75th percentiles) is calculated from maximum/minimum temperature and relative humidity data within a 5-day period centred on that day in the 30 years from 1991 to 2020.
The Probability of Significant Rain (PSR) forecast indicates the probability that accumulated rainfall generally over Hong Kong reaches 10 mm or more on that day.
10 mm is described as around the mean daily rainfall in rainy season.
For forecast elements other than PSR, average accuracy for the next one to three days is about 90%.
For forecast elements other than PSR, average accuracy for the four to seven days is about 85%, and for the eight to nine days about 80%.
The errors of PSR forecast in the next one to six days are within around 10%, and within around 20% for seven to nine days.
Weather in spring and summer, such as fog, tropical cyclones and severe convective weather, is more changeable, resulting in higher forecast uncertainty.
